Merge each task branch below into main, in the listed order, with
`git merge --squash <branch>`. Run every merge in the main checkout (`git rev-parse
--show-toplevel` of the repo, not a linked worktree), after `git checkout
main`. Touch nothing under `.radin/`.
You are a leaf: no user, no `AskUserQuestion`, no `Workflow`, no sub-agent of
your own. A skill that asks a human, or spawns and waits, hangs the router:
invoke none. One that starts asking, spawning or launching a workflow anyway:
stop invoking it and take the non-destructive path.
You get no background-task or `Monitor` notification: an ended turn is never
woken. Run every check in the foreground and wait for its exit in this turn:
never pass `run_in_background` or `Monitor` for a check. End only with your
`STATUS:` line.
Keep each tool call under 4 minutes: a longer one expires your 5-minute prompt
cache, and the next request writes your whole context again. Start a longer
command as `nohup <cmd> >"$TMPDIR/<name>.log" 2>&1 &`, then poll it in the
foreground inside the turn with repeated `timeout 240 sh -c 'while pgrep -f "<cmd>" >/dev/null; do sleep 5; done'` calls.
Never merge, rebase, reset or fast-forward a radin/* branch, yours or another
task's. If the tree lacks a dependency's work, end with STATUS: BLOCKED (FACT)
naming the dependency.

The branches are ones `radin state reconcile` could not merge cleanly. Merge each one whatever its task status: unfinished work lands too.

The branches, as `branch (task commit)`: radin/t-one (d7e4d84f6bdb).

A clean squash: commit it with `git commit -m "<the branch tip's subject>"`
(`git log -1 --format=%s <branch>`), then continue with the next branch.

A conflict: resolve it so both sides keep their intent, run the repo's checks
the conflicting files reach, and commit with the branch tip's subject. When the
two sides change the same behavior in ways that exclude each other, run `git
reset --merge`, leave that branch as it is, and report it as a decision. You never
pick between two product behaviors.

After a branch merges, remove its worktree (`git worktree remove <path>`, path
from `git worktree list`) and delete it with `git branch -D`, only once its squash
commit exists. Leave an unmerged branch and its worktree in place. Leave the checkout on main with a clean tree.

Your final message is exactly one of these lines, and nothing else:
`STATUS: SUCCESS — merged <branch list> into main at <tip hash>`
`STATUS: BLOCKED (DECISION) — <branch>: <the two behaviors in conflict>; merged <branch list, or "none">`
`STATUS: FAILED — <branch>, <why the merge or its checks failed>; merged <branch list, or "none">`
